that's right, the models implemented contain only lags, no exo. So you will have to modify the code, simply replacing the xx by your values. Let me know how that goes, I  might have some code for that.

PS: ccing the tsDyn mailing list

Matthieu

2013/5/30 Jor ge <jne...@hotmail.com>
> Hi Matthieu,
>
> I'm Jorge Neyro, an economist enrolled in the Master in Economics in the University of Buenos Aires.  I´ve started to do some research last year about Uncovered Interest Parity for the Argentine Economy using Logistic Smooth Transition Regression Models (LSTR) using Matlab. In this type of nonlinear model, I try to explain the rate of depreciation of the local currency (pesos argentinos) using the difference between local and foreign interest rates (exogenous variable). The objetive is to assess the accuracy of the forecast of rate of depreciation in the money market. More details here http://www.aaep.org.ar/anales/works/works2012/Neyro.pdf
>
> I want to use R and TsDyn to estimate those models and TVAR for my Master thesis. I´ve read carefully the TsDyn documentation and I didn´t find the possibility of estimate a non-linear model using only exogenous regressors as explanatory variables. Do you know how I can estimate such regression with TsDyn? Should I modify the TsDyn code?
>
> I really appreciate any help you can provide.
>
>
> Thanks
>
>
> Jorge Neyro
>
>

messages.subject: Re: three variables tvecm
messages.body_plain:
Hi Davide

This is a question that comes quite often, so I wrote a answer to it
on the FAQ: https://github.com/MatthieuStigler/tsDyn/wiki/FAQ
Please have a look, and in case a clarification/further question is
needed, don't hesitate to ask back on this list!

Best

Matthieu

On May 31, 12:33 pm, davidereat...@gmail.com wrote:
> Dear Matthieu Stigler,
>
>  I am a student in University of Padua Statistics' department, and I am
> working on my master thesis with R. I am analyzing the relathionship
> between three I(1) cointegrated variables. These variables are: electricity
> prices (Pel), exchange rate (Tc) and oil prices (Pp). Parametric test for
> Granger causality (based on VAR rappresentation of differentiated
> variables) doesn't report presence of causality. But if I implement Diks
> and Panchenko non parametric test for Granger causality I detect some
> causality between Pel and Tc. Moreover Hansen and Seo (2002) test for
> linear cointegration detects doubts about the linear cointegration hypothesis
> (p-value 0.02). So these signals of non-linearity lead me to TVECM representation.
> But how can I analyse these three variables jointly with a TVECM representation?
> I try to estimate bivariate TVECM with Pel and Tc and it highlights short
> run relationship that linear VECM doesn't highlight.So I think this can be
> a right approach for the problem but my goal is to consider all the three
> variables.
> Kind regards,
> Davide
>
>  results.docx
> 23KViewDownload
